I ran a paired t-test on new-book prices, since each textbook has both a bookstore price and an Amazon price. I used the 68 books that have both prices. The test gives t = 2.20 with 67 degrees of freedom and a two-sided p-value of 0.0312. That is below 0.05, so there is evidence of a difference in average price between the UCLA bookstore and Amazon.

An unpaired (independent-samples) t-test on all available prices gives p = 0.0512. I chose the paired version because the two prices describe the same books.

ANSWER: 0.0312
